from.place: proof step (1): the projection map and its isomorphism property are local on an open cover of Y

title: Locality of the projection-formula isomorphism
statement: Let f:X\to Y be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let E be an object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) and K an object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category] [def-pc-derived-pullback] [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and let U_i be an open covering of Y. The canonical map Rf_*(E)\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}^{\mathbb L}K\to Rf_*(E\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbb L}Lf^*K) is an isomorphism if and only if its restriction to each f^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i is an isomorphism.

source.place: Equation 20.54.2.1 (cohomology-equation-projection-formula-map); locality assertion used in perfect.tex Lemma 36.22.1 (Tag 08EU)

proof.text: Fix i, write V=U_i, U=f^{-1}(V) and g=f|_U:U\to V. By [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde] (1) there are canonical isomorphisms (Lf^*K)|_U\cong Lg^*(K|_V), (E\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{\mathcal O_X}Lf^*K)|_U\cong E|_U\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{\mathcal O_U}(Lf^*K)|_U and (Rf_*E\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{\mathcal O_Y}K)|_V\cong (Rf_*E)|_V\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{\mathcal O_V}K|_V; by [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] there are canonical isomorphisms (Rf_*E)|_V\cong Rg_*(E|_U) and (Rf_*(E\otimes^{\mathbb L}Lf^*K))|_V\cong Rg_*((E\otimes^{\mathbb L}Lf^*K)|_U). The canonical map (Cohomology, Equation 20.54.2.1) is adjoint to Lf^*(Rf_*E\otimes^{\mathbb L}K)\cong Lf^*Rf_*E\otimes^{\mathbb L}Lf^*K\to E\otimes^{\mathbb L}Lf^*K, built from the counit of Lf^*\dashv Rf_*; these identifications are natural and compatible with the unit and counit, so under them the restriction of the canonical map for f to V is the canonical map for g applied to E|_U and K|_V (a diagram chase).

A morphism \varphi in D(\mathcal O_Y) is an isomorphism exactly when H^q(\varphi) is an isomorphism of sheaves of \mathcal O_Y-modules for every q (its cone is acyclic). Restriction to an open subscheme is exact, so H^q(\varphi)|_{U_i}=H^q(\varphi|_{U_i}). A morphism of sheaves of modules is an isomorphism if and only if its restriction to each member of an open covering is one (its kernel and cokernel are sheaves, zero when zero on a cover). Hence, by step 1, the canonical map for f is an isomorphism exactly when the canonical map for each f^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i is.
